Supplementary table legends

Table S1 Cell line and perturbation compound information

A. Cell line annotations used in this study, including source, catalog number, cancer subtype,
gene mutations and proliferation rates measured over 48 h log-phase culture.

B. Perturbation annotations used in this study, including the perturbation ID, drug name,
catalog number, CAS number, SMILES structure, known molecular targets, associated
pathways, and drug subtypes. The final column provides target protein names and their
corresponding UniProt IDs. The "Target" column reports target annotations from the drug
datasheets, which in some cases refer to broad target families rather than individual proteins.
To provide protein-level annotations, we manually curated the corresponding drug target
proteins and UniProt IDs from DrugBank (https://go.drugbank.com); these are listed in the
final target protein/UniProt ID columns. Drug_type1 and drug_type2 are DrugBank-based
classifications, with Drug_type1 indicating the broad therapeutic or mechanistic class and
Drug_type2 indicating the more specific target or mechanism class.

C. This table summarizes the cell viability assays used to determine drug efficacy based on
the 24 h response. Drug responses were labelled as resistant (N) or sensitive (Y) according to
the efficacy criteria described in the Methods. Each cell viability assay was performed with
three biological replicates. Detailed criteria for defining drug efficacy are provided in the
Methods. Compound #3 was available only in limited quantity; therefore, its drug efficacy
was not measured, and it was excluded from subsequent model training and evaluation.

Table S2 Sample metadata and proteomic profiles for mtPTDS

A. Sample-level metadata for 2487 non-pooled mtPTDS proteomic samples from the
mtPTDS dataset, collected across 11 perturbation times (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 24, 36, 48, and
60 h) in three TNBC cell lines (HCC1806, HCC1143 and MDA-MB-453-1). Metadata
include sample ID, cell line, cell plate ID, perturbation time, treatment category, drug or
combination ID, anchor and library drug ID and doses, MS instrument and replicate type.
Drug identifiers are indexed in Table S1B. The table includes 2354 independent samples, 84
technical replicates and 49 biological replicates; pooled QC samples are not included in this
table. Technical replicates, biological replicates and pooled samples were used for quality
control and reproducibility assessment.

B. Matched protein abundance matrix for these 2487 samples. Rows correspond to samples

Table S7 Compound information, efficacy labels and model evaluation on the PTNC
dataset

A. Information on the 81 compounds included in the PTNC dataset. Compounds were
indexed by their corresponding Pert_IDs and were purchased from TargetMol. The table
includes compound name, catalog number, CAS number, SMILES, molecular formula,
pathway annotations, indication, solvent, target annotations and drug type.

                                                                     3

B. This table summarizes the cell viability assays used to determine compound efficacy based
on the 24 h response. Each cell viability assay was performed with three biological replicates.
Drug responses were labelled as resistant (N; negative class) or sensitive (Y; positive class)
according to the efficacy criteria described in the Methods. Cell-line-compound combinations
with inconsistent labels across repeated experiments were removed; therefore, the resulting
compound-by-cell-line matrix is not fully orthogonal.

C. AUPRC, AUROC, and accuracy of different models tested on the PTNC dataset. For the
scFM baselines, predictions from multiple random-seed runs showed near-constant outputs
across samples (prediction collapse). Accordingly, their AUPRC values were close to the
positive-class prevalence baseline in this dataset.

D. Comparison of significant differences between ProteinTalks and other models.

Table S8 Sample metadata, compound information and proteomic profiles for PTPC.

A. Sample-level metadata for the PTPC dataset, an independent perturbation proteomics
dataset generated across five cancer cell lines (A375, HCT116, NCI-H1975, NCI-H2170 and
Panc 10.05). Proteomic profiles were collected at 6 h and 24 h after treatment, with control
samples assigned a perturbation time of 0 h. This table lists 2217 non-pooled samples,
comprising 2021 independent proteomic samples and 196 technical or biological replicates.
The 90 pooled samples are included in the total PTPC sample count but are not listed in this
table. After accounting for pooled and replicate samples, PTPC contained 2021 independent
proteomic samples for model evaluation.

B. Compound information for the 716 perturbation identifiers used in PTPC, corresponding to
708 unique compound names. All compounds were purchased from TargetMol. Information
includes perturbation ID, catalog number, compound name, CAS number, SMILES,
molecular formula, pathway annotations, indication, solvent, target annotations and
compound type.

and anti-RCOR3 (1:100, AP55371, Abcepta). After washing, sections were incubated with
HRP-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG polymer (PV-6001, ZSGB-BIO) at 37�C for 30 min,
followed by 3,3'-Diaminobenzidine (DAB) chromogen development and hematoxylin
counterstaining.
Staining was independently scored by two experienced pathologists blinded to clinical
information, using the H-score method 10. Each section was evaluated for staining intensity on
a scale of 0-3 (0, negative; 1, weak; 2, moderate; 3, strong) and the percentage of positive
tumor cells on a scale of 1-4 (1, 25%; 2, 26-50%; 3, 51-75%; 4, >75%). The H-score was
calculated as the product of these two parameters, yielding a total score ranging from 0 to 12.
Samples were classified as negative (0), low (1-4), moderate (5-8), or high (9-12)
expressors.
